newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London steady to firm, await FOMC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London steady to firm, await FOMC.

text.p: U.S. shares were slightly higher on balance following Wall Street's advance on Tuesday but trading volumes remained light as investors awaited news from the U.S. Federal Reserve on interest rates.
"The market doesn't expect any rate changes but there is always that nagging doubt," one market maker said.
"The Fed has slipped in a rate rise and caught the market off guard before."
The FOMC meeting concludes later today. Any change to the the U.S. short-term funds rate would not normally be expected until after 1915 GMT/1415 EST, dealers said.

U.S. treasuries were steady after rising on Tuesday for the seventh-straight day. The yield on the 30-year long bond was standing at 6.71 percent, its lowest rate since December 31, when it touched 6.64 percent.
The March T-bond was up 3/32 at 112-10/32 by 1115 GMT. The S&P 500 futures contract was up 0.80 to 794.50.

Cisco Systems was trading at $66 versus a New York close of $67-1/8 after the company reported second-quarter earnings of $0.49 per share compared with a First Call consensus estimate of $0.50. The results were released after Wall Street's official finish.
Goodyear Tire was $3/8 higher at $55-5/8 after press reports that the company had entered a strategic alliance with Sumitomo Rubber Industries.
McDonalds Corp was up $1/8 at $46 following news that U.S. investment strategist Elaine Garzarelli had tipped the share to outperform the S&P 500 by 30 to 40 percent in 1997.

Elsewhere, Pepsi was up $1/8 at $33 after dropping $1-1/4 in the U.S. on Tuesday after reporting disappointing Q4 earnings. "We've seen a bit of bottom-fishing in Pepsi but no great volumes," one dealer said.
